1  JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 10.10.2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 10.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m. the petitioner was riding his two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA-41-EC- 4365 from Halapanagudde side towards Kunigal side, while so traveling on NH-75 road, in front of Halapanagudde Masidi, Yadiyuru Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkuru District,

at that time, the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 came from Nademavinapura gate side towards Kunigal side in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Motorcycle of the petitioner from back side and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to CHC Kunigal Hospital,
Kunigal, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Sree Siddartha Hospital,
Tumakuru wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery and discharged with an advice to come for further treatment.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was aged about 64 years, doing labour work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the accidental injuries petitioner became permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-
with interest.
3. After service of summons, both the respondents have appeared through their counsels, and respondent No.2 insurer filed written statement.
But, respondent No.1 -owner not choosen to file written statement.
The respondent No.2- insurance company filed written statement by admitting issuance of policy in respect of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 and also the petitioner were not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident, the petitioner's age,
occupation, income and injuries suffered by him.

By denying the involvement and also the Giriyappa vs Shanthamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89183845/
2 negligence of the offending Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.
The respondent No.2-insurance company has also filed additional written statement by denying the involvement of the offending Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB- 9351.

Further this respondent submits that the complainant has clearly and voluntarily given statement before the Hospital authorities that the alleged accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HB-7351 (falsely inserted Bike to Bike in MLC) and said fact has not been intimated to concerned police authorities, however the complainant was an afterthought has filed a false complaint colluding with the police authorities and owner of the vehicle more than 28 days after the said accident.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievious injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HB-9351 by its rider, in RTA took place on 10.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m on NH-75 road, in front of Halappanagudde Ma- sidi, Yadiyuru Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkuru District?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 11.
Further examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P12 to Ex.P14.
The respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R9.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 :
As per final orders  for the following:-

: R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :

3 8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report and Charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the petitioner at Kunigal police station by alleging the rash and negligent riding by the rider of Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
In continuation the IO conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.
On perusal of Ex.P3 the accident spot is in the northern edge of the road.
Further the Ex.P6 IMV report shows that the motorcycle of the petitioner has got damages in its front right side corner shape, right side rider foot panel bent.
On the other hand the offending motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 has got damages in its front left side corner shape, left side rider foot panel, bent and left side steering handle bent.

The content of Ex.P3 and 6 prima facie establishes the negligence of the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB- 9351.
10.

After the investigation and after examining the eye witness and investigating officer filed charge sheet as per Ex.P7 by opining that the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.

Thereby these documents produced by the petitioner helped the petitioner to primafacie establish his case and to show the negligence of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
11.
The respondent No.2 insurer filed written statement and also examined its official as RW.1.
The Rw.1 filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination wherein as admitted by the RW.1 his evidence is based on the document specially on crime records.
The crime records and opinion of I.O. point outs the negligence of the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
No independent evidence is placed to deny the opinion of the I.O. as per Ex.P7.

It is the contention of the respondent No.2 insurance company that the petitioner before the hospital authorities given statement by stating that the accident was caused by the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-7351 but later stage the false case was registered against the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
To overcome the said defence the petitioner summoned the MLC register extract which is marked at Ex.P12 and the author of the Ex.P12 also examined by the petitioner as PW2.

12 . The PW2 who wrote the Ex.P12 MLC register extract deposed before this court that as per Ex.P12 petitioner gave information about the accident and as per the said entry the offending vehicle number is KA-06-HB- 9351.
Thereby by examining the author of Ex.P12 the petitioner gave clarification that the accident was occurred between the bike and bike and the offending vehicle number is KA-06-HB-9351.
By this the involvement of the vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 stands established.
13. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
The PW.1 was cross-
examined at length by denying the negligence of the rider of Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 but nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Thus, it can be concluded that, the negligence was on the part of the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.

Giriyappa vs Shanthamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89183845/
4 14.
Ex.P7 charge sheet was also came to be filed on the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner and also to disbelieve the contents of charge sheet.
15. As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident was caused by the negligent act by the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
16.
The respondent No.2 insurance company even though filed written statement, has failed to establish the negligence on the part of petitioner for the occurrence of the accident.
The charge sheet was came to be filed on the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 of IPC.

2009 ACJ 287 (National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

17. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular Car in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

19. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.

20. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 28 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly, instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought and the offending vheilce is Giriyappa vs Shanthamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89183845/
5 implicated in the case even though it is not involved in the accident.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioners doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 10.10.2022 at about 6.30 p.m., but the FIR was lodged on 08.11.2022 at about 7,15 p.m., and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after 28 days of occurrence of the accident.

But the informant in the Ex.P2 first information it is stated that soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to hospital and underwent the surgery and also as there was no one to look after the petitioner, they were unable to give the complaint immediately.

Along with this the petitioner also produced Ex.P12 MLC register extract wherein it is stated that the petitioner met with an accident on 10.10.2022 wherein the accident was between bike and bike and the vehicle bearing No.KA-06- HB-9351 is involved in the accident.
Thereafter as per Ex.P8 the petitioner admitted Siddartha Hospital on 10.10.2022 and discharged on 28.10.2022.
Thereby it shows that the petitioner sustained injuries in RTA dated 10.10.2022 and he was not able to give complaint as he was under the treatment.
The Ex.p12 MLC register extract shows that on 10.10.2022 the petitioner met with an accident and KA-06-HB-9351 caused the accident.
These documents supported the case of the petitioner regarding the occurrence of accident.
Further the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 also discloses that on the date of accident itself the petitioner was admitted to their hospital with an history of RTA.
The endeavor of the injured usually will be getting the treatment to the injured than thinking about the legal formalities.

Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me)

In the judgment reported in 2011 ACJ 911 between Ravi V/s.
Badrinarayan and others, wherein it is held as follows;

sentences.text:
The cumulative effect of the aforesaid events clearly established that accident had taken place on 7.10.2001 at about 8.30 in the morning on account of rash and negligent reversing of the truck by driver Badrinarayan, owned by Respondent No. 2,
Prahlad Singh.
Under these circumstances, it cannot be said that delay in lodging the FIR could have proved fatal to the claim case filed by Ravi.
19. Narration of the aforesaid events would show the bonafides of Suresh.
As mentioned herein above, a consistent stand has been taken right from the beginning till the lodging of the FIR.

The chronological events narrated herein above inspire confidence and it does not smack of a concocted case which has been filed against the driver and the owner of the vehicle only with an intention to get compensation.
20. It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

22. In the case in hand, the Claims Tribunal as well as the High Court, committed grave error in not appeciating the mental agony through which Suresh was passing,
whose son was severely injured.

Giriyappa vs Shanthamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89183845/
7 23.

In the light of the aforesaid discussion, we are of the considered opinion that the MACT as well as High Court committed error in coming to the conclusion that lodging the FIR belatedly would result in dismissal of the claim petition".

21. Further the respondent No.2 insurance company also produced copy of the B register extract of vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-7351 and copy of insurance policy of vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-7351 as per Ex.R4 and R5.
As per Ex.R4 and R5 as on the date of accident the vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-7351 had no valid existing insurance policy.
Only on the basis of this document it cannot be said that vehicle bearing No.KA- 06-HB-7351 caused the accident and not vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
As stated by the PW2 who is author of Ex.P12 MLC register extract the number of offending vehicle forthcoming in Ex.P12 MLC register extract is vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
Thereby the oral and documentary evidence of PW2 and Ex.P12 MLC register extract shows that the vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB- 9351 caused the accident and not vehicle
bearing

. Hence the delay of 28 days, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint, Ex.P12- MLC and Ex.P8 discharge summary it cannot be considered as inordinate.
22. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10.10.2022 which was caused by the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 which belongs to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
23.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which was caused by the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06- HB-9351.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 64 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P11 the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1956.
The accident was took place on 10.10.2022.
Hence as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 66 years 9 months 9 days.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 and discharge summary at Ex.P8.

As per Ex.P8 the petitioner was admitted to Sree Siddhartha Hospital, Tumkuru wherein petitioner took treatment for the injuries sustained i.e., Bicondylar fracture right proximal tibia cschetzar MPC as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
By considering the nature of injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

Giriyappa vs Shanthamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89183845/
8 b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bill as per Ex.P10 amounting to Rs.2,26,755/-.
The medical bill is not seriously disputed by the respondents and no grounds are made out to disbelieve these bill.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.2,27,000/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was a doing Labour work and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any documents.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered in the year 2022 at Rs.15,500/- p.m.

As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8 - the petitioner was admitted to Sree Siddhartha Hospital , Tumakuru from 10.10.2022 to 28.10.2022, again from 10.01.2023 to 14.01.2023, from 16.03.2023 to 25.03.2023 and at Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, Mandya from 08.04.2023 to 04.05.2023 in total for a period of 61 days.

entities.text: Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Centre, Mandya
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total 5 months period including 61 days inpatient period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500 X 5 months = Rs.77,500/- during the laid up period.
d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner has examined Dr.
Ramesh B., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital
as PW.3
and through him clinical notes and X-rays were got marked at Ex.P13 and Ex.P14.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained bicondylar fracture right proximal tibia.
As per the evidence of PW3 doctor the petitioner sustained lower limb disability of 40% and whole body disability of 20%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to some extent.
The fracture is mal-united and implants are already removed.

A perusal of the injuries sustained,
treatment taken, it is considered that though the petitioner is having permanent physical whole body disability of 20%.
Hence considering all these aspects this tribunal has taken disability at 15%.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '5'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 5 X 15% =Rs.1,39,500/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P8 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 61 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
By considering the nature of the injury and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injury sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 61 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the fracture as discussed above, it Giriyappa vs Shanthamma on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89183845/
9 may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.61,000/- in total as the petitioner has spent 61 days in the hospital.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 has not stated that petitioner needs any surgery in future.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a. Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000/- b.

Towards medical expenses Rs. 2,27,000/-
c.

Towards loss of income during Rs. 77,500/-
laid up period
d. Towards disability Rs. 1,39,500/- e.

Towards food, nourishment and Rs. 20,000/-
conveyance f.
Towards attendant charges Rs. 61,000/- g.

Towards loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-
h.
Towards future medical expenses Nil
. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
25.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:

10 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,90,000/- (Rupees Five lakh ninety thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of the amount awarded, it is ordered to release the entire compensation amount to the petitioner.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 10.10.2022.
Further contended that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 and also the petitioner were not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioners doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

The chronological events narrated herein above inspire confidence and it does not smack of a concocted case which has been filed against the driver and the owner of the vehicle only with an intention to get compensation.
20. It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.
If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.
In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.
22. In the case in hand, the Claims Tribunal as well as the High Court, committed grave error in not appeciating the mental agony through which Suresh was passing,
whose son was severely injured.
As per Ex.R4 and R5 as on the date of accident the vehicle bearing No.KA-06-HB-7351 had no valid existing insurance policy.
22. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 10.10.2022 which was caused by the rider of the Bike bearing No.KA-06-HB-9351 which belongs to respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
The petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident.

ISSUE NO.3:
25.
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.5,90,000/- (Rupees Five lakh ninety thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2- insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Draw up award accordingly.
